Team — I pulled the AWS marketplace settlement export for March and attached a sanitized CSV showing all settlement lines for RWD-0009. Summary:

- Total gross usage reported by AWS: $18,500
- Marketplace fees & taxes: $2,200
- Redwood-issued promo credit applied (REDWOOD_PROMO): $4,200 (applied on 2026-03-25)
- Platform-level metering adjustment: -$200 (applied 2026-03-29 as a correction to a previous over-reporting)
- Net to customer shown on invoice: $12,100

However — AWS separately applied a tax rounding adjustment of +$300 on their invoice (line: TAX_ROUNDING_ADJ) which is why ClearLake is seeing $12,400 on the invoice PDF. That rounding happens when AWS aggregates per-transaction VAT and then normalizes to the invoice currency; it's rare but not unheard of.

I've attached: aws_marketplace_settlement_2026-03.csv and a short audit workbook (redwood_credit_audit_2026-03.xlsx) where I mapped promo-credit IDs to customer accounts. Looks like ClearLake did receive REDWOOD_PROMO for the majority of their usage — the $200 correction was already included in our internal export but AWS part of the rounding adj was not visible in the customer's usage CSV.

Next actions I recommend:
1) Send ClearLake the settlement CSV + our audit workbook showing the mapping (so they can reconcile to their export).
2) Confirm VAT-exemption stamps on AWS side. If AWS accepted the exemption after the invoice cut, AWS can issue a VAT refund/credit to the customer — we can supply evidence to accelerate that.
3) If the customer still disputes the $300, offer a one-time goodwill credit while we pursue the AWS rounding reversal (quick customer retention play).
